sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Exec: INSERT UPDATE DELETE] --> R[result: rows affected]
    Q[Query: SELECT many] --> ROWS[rows cursor — iterate + Close]
    QR[QueryRow: SELECT one] → SCAN[Scan directly]
    PARAM[? parameters] → SAFE[injection-proof]
    CONCAT[string concat] → INJECT[SQL injection]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The pool and the lazy connection: sql.Open doesn't connect — it validates the config and returns immediately. The first Query/Exec pulls a connection from the pool (creating it if needed). The pool tuning: SetMaxOpenConns (the DB's ceiling — Postgres default 100, your app should take a fraction), SetMaxIdleConns (the kept-open connections), SetConnMaxLifetime (the cutover-safe recycling — DB failovers are invisible to the app).

The Rows mechanics: Query returns a live cursor — each Next() fetches from the connection. The connection is on loan for the iteration's duration (an unclosed Rows holds a pool connection hostage — the production pool-exhaustion bug). Close releases it — ALWAYS deferred.

The NULL discipline: a nullable column can't Scan into a non-pointer — Scan into sql.NullString / sql.NullInt64 (the type with Value + Valid), or use COALESCE in the query (SELECT COALESCE(email, '') ...). The NULL-to-interface{} trap (Scan into *interface{} gets []byte, not string — the driver-specific encoding surprise).
